query: Based on these observations, one can speculate that the connectivity between the OB and its targets in the olfactory cortex may occur by two different mechanisms. Genetic factors, including lineage, may contribute to the connectivity between M/T cells and the amygdala, as this brain area is involved in innate behavior responses that may require hardwired connections (Sosulski et al., 2011). In contrast, the connectivity between M/T cells and areas of the olfactory cortex involved in the perception of odors that do not elicit innate behaviors are more plastic and may be regulated by mechanisms independent of lineage, such as random neurite targeting and activity-dependent wiring, among others (Caron et al., 2013; Schaffer et al., 2018).
